about.title: Palos Verdes Estates Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Palos Verdes Estates is a quiet, hillside community, but its terraced yards, ocean-view walkways, and older commercial buildings along Palos Verdes Drive West create their own set of fall hazards — uneven pavers, loose gravel on sloped paths, and slick tile near coastal-facing entries. When a fall happens on someone else's property, California law generally requires you to show the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to fix it or warn you. That's why documenting the scene matters right after it happens, whether the incident occurred in a hillside shopping area, a private residence, or a public building. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise any result; we simply connect injured residents and visitors with an independent attorney in our network who can review the facts, gather evidence such as surveillance footage, and advise on next steps. The consultation and connection are free, and attorneys work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Fall

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California premises liability claims generally require showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and didn't fix or warn about it. An attorney can help identify how long a hazard existed and whether prior complaints or inspection records support your claim.

items.title: Video and Evidence Disappear Fast
items.desc: Surveillance footage from stores, HOA-managed common areas, or nearby businesses is often overwritten within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of that footage can be critical to showing what actually happened.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, so even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help present the facts in a way that fairly reflects what happened.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Palos Verdes Estates?
items.answer: In California, you generally have two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit for injuries on someone else's property. If the property involved is owned or maintained by a public entity — such as a city-owned park or municipal building — the deadline is much shorter and requires a formal claim first. Because these timelines are strict, it helps to speak with an attorney as soon as possible after the incident.

items.question: What if my fall happened on a private residence in the hillside area?
items.answer: Homeowners in Palos Verdes Estates, like any property owner, can be held responsible if they knew or should have known about a hazard, such as an uneven walkway or broken step, and failed to address it. Photos of the specific condition, along with witness names, can help support your case. An independent attorney can evaluate whether the facts fit California's notice requirement.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent attorneys in our network. Those attorneys work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation, and there's no cost to you for the initial connection.
